format: 16-team Superflex Dynasty · Full PPR · no taxi squad

classRead.summary: A WR-heavy class with a historically weak QB crop. Fernando Mendoza is the only QB worth a first-round rookie pick (top-3 in Superflex); Carson Beck and the rest are Round-3 values. Five WRs went in Round 1 of the NFL draft, eight in the first two rounds — the strength of this class is exactly where your picks are NOT, so the play at 15/16 is the second WR tier, a falling RB, or a trade.
classRead.qbNote: Do NOT reach for a rookie QB at 15/16 — it's a bad class. Solve Superflex QB via the vet market (Flacco went for a 2nd in this league last October).
classRead.noTaxiNote: No taxi squad: year-one usability matters. A redshirt project burns an active roster spot all season.

myRosterRead.core: Bijan Robinson (2023 1.02) is the franchise. Cooper Kupp (acquired from the Machines, Aug 2024) is aging out — a young-WR succession piece is the biggest need.
myRosterRead.qb: QB room thin since the Dak trade (Nov 2024, to Porkys for two 1sts). Mac Jones came back in the Jonnu Smith deal. Superflex hole — but fix it with a vet trade, not this class.
myRosterRead.strategy: 15: highest-floor PPR WR (Branch). 16: best available RB to pair with Bijan, or Douglas if you want the WR ceiling swing. Do not draft a QB. Consider trading 16 down into Round 2 (Douglas/Bell/Thompson range) plus a future pick if a partner wants back in.

tradeNotes: Moving up: the cost is steep and the board says you don't need to — your targets (Branch tier) live at 13-18, not 8-12. Only move up if a Tier-2 WR (Concepcion/Boston/Williams) slides past 10 and the Machines start circling.
Moving down from 16: strong play. 16 → early 20s keeps you in the Douglas/Stowers range and adds capital. Beaver Eaters (21/23/26) and PCE (28/30/31) are the natural partners.

Keith rule: any faller you want, assume Keith at 17 wants him too — that's the real deadline on your 15/16 decisions and the reason NOT to get cute trading down past 17 with a target still on the board.
